en.intro: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen for one Sanskrit word that shows exactly why a person cannot become a yogi.
en.notice: The word sankalpa, intention, is the only inner obstacle to becoming a yogi. Krishna says that without dropping these inner intentions, no one becomes a yogi, and true renunciation is simply giving up these intentions.
en.next: Krishna now explains that action is the way up, but stillness is the way to stay there.
en.meaning: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अर्जुन से एक ऐसे शब्द को सुनने के लिए कहते हैं जो यह बताता है कि कोई व्यक्ति योगी क्यों नहीं बन सकता।
hi.meaning: हे अर्जुन, जिसे लोग संन्यास कहते हैं, उसी को तुम योग समझो। क्योंकि मन में उठने वाले संकल्पों को छोड़े बिना कोई भी व्यक्ति योगी नहीं हो सकता।
hi.notice: शब्द है सङ्कल्प, यानी इरादा, जो योगी बनने में एकमात्र भीतरी बाधा है। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि बिना इन भीतरी संकल्पों को छोड़े कोई भी योगी नहीं बन सकता, और सच्चा संन्यास इन्हीं भीतरी संकल्पों का त्याग ही है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब समझाते हैं कि योग में ऊपर जाने के लिए कर्म साधन है, लेकिन योग में स्थापित होने के लिए शांति साधन है।

en.intro: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen for one Sanskrit word that shows exactly why a person cannot become a yogi.
en.body: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions. The word sankalpa, intention, is the only inner obstacle to becoming a yogi. Krishna says that without dropping these inner intentions, no one becomes a yogi, and true renunciation is simply giving up these intentions. Krishna now explains that action is the way up, but stillness is the way to stay there.

issues: borrowed: "The word is sankalpa, intention." (The phrase 'The word is sankalpa, intention' is a direct translation of the Hindi 'शब्द है सङ्कल्प, यानी इरादा' from the notice section. However, the notice section is meant to explain the verse's meaning, not to introduce the word. More importantly, the notice states 'true renunciation is not about giving up fire or work,' which is a concept explicitly attributed to the PREVIOUS verse (verse 1) in the source, not this one. This misattributes the previous verse's content to the current notice.)

borrowed: "सच्चा संन्यास मन की सभी योजनाओं को त्यागने का ही नाम है" (The Hindi notice presents content from the NEXT verse (verse 3, which discusses 'stillness is the means') as if it were in this verse. The source for this verse only mentions giving up sankalpa (intention), not 'peace/stillness' (shanti) as the defining act of true renunciation. The English notice also incorrectly frames 'true renunciation' as leaving behind all inner plans, which is a paraphrase of verse 1, not the core meaning of this specific verse.)
